rows.rule: UETA section 10 error-correction affordance: before Complete the signer reviews the frozen pages and the values they filled in, and can still correct them. The ceremony's review-before-complete step is this row.

source.citation: Uniform Electronic Transactions Act (1999) section 10, Effect of change or error; ARCH-0064 section 8

rows.rule: UETA section 14 and ESIGN 15 U.S.C. 7001(h): a contract formed by an electronic agent is valid, so an agent that prepares and sends while a human signs is settled law.

source.citation: Uniform Electronic Transactions Act (1999) section 14; 15 U.S.C. 7001(h); ARCH-0064 section 8

rows.rule: eIDAS regulates how a signature is created, not who dispatches the request, so an agent sending is untouched. A deployment may add disclosure rows here; the SES, AES or QES tier is a document setting, not an engine wall.

Under the 2020 witness-type Q&A each signer's own click is the signer's own intent, so the Art. 3 presumption holds. An agent that performs the sign act forfeits it, which is why the sign-action dial stays closed by default (D6).

source.citation: Act on Electronic Signatures and Certification Business (Act No. 102 of 2000) Art. 3; 2020 ministry Q&A on witness-type e-contract services; ARCH-0064 section 8

rows.rule: Art. 72 (non-lawyer legal services) matters only if signing is offered to others as a service. A note, not a v1 constraint.

source.citation: Attorney Act (Act No. 205 of 1949) Art. 72; ARCH-0064 section 8
